chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)

Regarding a man who gave a man dirhams to perform Hajj on his behalf as a solitary Hajj, it is permissible for him to perform Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj). He said: 'Yes, he only differed for the sake of preference (or extra reward).'

key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: To perform Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: Can a person who pays someone else to perform Hajj for them also perform Umrah themselves?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies that a person who commissions another to perform Hajj on their behalf retains the right to perform Umrah al-Tamattu' themselves, as the agent's performance fulfills the obligation without invalidating the payer's concurrent ritual status. Scholars interpret the phrase 'only for the sake of preference' (innama khalaqa ila al-fadl) to indicate that while the Hajj is valid, the payer may choose the more meritorious or easier mode of worship for themselves, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding delegated acts of worship.
